newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market calmer at end week.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market calmer at end week.

text.p: Activity was subdued on the sugar freight market on Thursday with few new orders emerging and no great changes in reported rates, shipbrokers said. "It's fairly quiet," said one broker, adding that little major new business was expected before the end of the week.
CSR was open for 14,850 tonnes of bulk sugar for its usual Queensland stem to Praia Mole for 20/30 September.
CSR also fixed 17,000 tonnes in bulk from the same port to Japan for September 15/25 at a reported rate of $18.25.
Shipbrokers said E D & F Man issued an order recently for 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to the Black Sea for 10/30 September.
Other reported fixtures included Mauritius Sugar Syndicate with 14,250/14,500 tonnes min/max bulk sugar on its usual Port Louis to London run at stg 16.00.
Elsewhere, Syria issued an international tender for September 4 to buy 26,000 tonnes of white sugar and 26,000 tonnes of raws for October/November delivery to replace a cancelled tender.
Both the amounts should be delivered between October 10 and November 10 in two equal cargoes of 13,000 tonnes each.
Pakistan is said to be considering buying another 200,000 tonnes of refined crystal white sugar for delivery in September and October.
